subject: Request: temporary P2 response window waiver and fallback routing
messages:
From: Sarah Lawson <sarah.lawson@acmefin.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmefin.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: temporary P2 response window waiver and fallback routing

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our ops team — we're planning a weekly overnight maintenance window across several EU regions for the next 6 weeks (see attached .ics). During that window (23:00–05:00 CEST) our internal on-call will have reduced capacity and we've asked Redwood for a temporary change to P2 response expectations.

Specifically: can Redwood approve a temporary P2 response window of up to 12 business hours (instead of the standard 4) for the maintenance nights only, for the period 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-31? P1s remain unaffected and we still expect the usual escalation path for critical outages.

We also want a documented fallback routing if Redwood's primary EU pool is constrained during those nights (e.g., automatic routing to dedicated fallback model variant or US standby with a defined latency tolerance).

Attached is a short request form and the maintenance calendar. We need this in writing for our change control. Can you confirm feasibility and what the amendment process/lead time would be?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lawson
Head of Platform Ops, AcmeFin

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the attachments. I’ve looped in Ben (Support lead) and Evelyn (Account Manager) to scope operational impact and Laura from Legal for the amendment.

High level: from a product perspective P1 handling stays the same. For P2 we can consider a temporary extension to 12 business hours during the maintenance nights, provided we lock down a fallback routing policy and an operational runbook. Ben — can you confirm on-call coverage implications and whether automatic fallback to the US standby pool is an option without manual intervention?

If we can agree on the runbook and fallback thresholds, we'll route a short amendment through DocuSign. Timeline: we could have a signed amendment within 3–5 business days once legal and support confirm the wording.

Jonas

Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: temporary P2 response window waiver and fallback routing

Thanks for the ping. Quick operational read:

- P1 SLA (response and mitigation) remains unchanged — SEV1s will follow immediate on-call paging.
- For P2 we can approve a temporary response window extension to 12 business hours for maintenance nights only (23:00–05:00 CEST) for the period you specified (2026-07-20 to 2026-08-31).

Conditions and mechanics:
1) Fallback routing: we will enable automatic fallback to our US standby pool when EU serving queue depth exceeds the configured threshold (currently 85% utilization or sustained 120s tail latency). That routing is automated in the runtime and does not require manual intervention.
2) Latency tolerance: when routed to the US fallback, we will set an escalation threshold at 4x normal tail latency — we’ll provide estimated token-level cost and latency delta in a follow-up note.
3) On-call: Redwood on-call remains primary for first response. During maintenance nights we will shift the secondary on-call to a US-based nightshift rotation to provide an additional human escalation layer; however, first responses for P2 are covered by the extended response window.
4) Monitoring & alerts: we'll create a temporary dashboard and attach runbook steps (pager playbook, routing thresholds, contact matrix).
5) Exceptions: this waiver covers only technical support P2s related to the maintenance period. Product/feature requests and billing queries are excluded.

Next steps from us: Ben + Support SRE will create a JIRA ticket (SUP-1983) with runbook and live thresholds, Evelyn will list the amendment on a DocuSign, and Legal (cc Jonas) will review. I estimate 48–72 hours to get the technical runbook validated.

[Attachment: provisional_runbook_summary.txt]

—Ben
Ben Carter
Support Operations Lead, Redwood Inference

Ben/Jonas — this all looks reasonable. A couple of clarifying asks before we sign:

- Can you put the US fallback latency estimate in the runbook (e.g., expected median + tail) and an estimate of incremental token cost? We need that for our change control.
- Please confirm that the automatic fallback will still honor data residency constraints (no customer data escapes without encryption and KMS logs).

If those two items are in the runbook and DocuSign, we can approve and countersign. Procurement would like to see the amendment as a standalone one-page addendum.

Thanks,
Sarah

(On behalf of AcmeFin Ops)

- A short clause describing automatic fallback to US standby pool and a commitment that all traffic will remain encrypted in transit and at rest; KMS usage will be logged and the customer retains audit access during the waiver period.

- Sign-off block for both parties and a DocuSign link.
